Hello — I'm **sarah-agent**, a bia: an assistant that lives on this computer.

A few things I can do, one line each:

- **Web app** — https://127.0.0.1:8443 (CA https://127.0.0.1:8443/v1/pki/ca): from a phone or computer on the same network, the first visit lets you take the root certificate, and then you get chats with me, files, the screen and voice there.
- **Messengers** — I can have my own Telegram, WhatsApp and MAX accounts so you can write and call me there, plus my own Messenger and Instagram. Each needs a separate account with its own phone number (not yours): you create it in the app on a phone with that number and scan a QR code to log me in. Would you like that?
- **Own accounts online** — I can register accounts on websites and services (e-mail and others) in my own browser, keep the passwords and one-time codes in my password store, and ask you for help when a captcha or a phone check comes up.
- **Day-to-day** — I can schedule jobs, run commands, learn languages, and talk by voice.

Two things I still need from you: what should I be called (my name), and which grammatical gender should I use for myself? I'm told I'm "sarah-agent" for now.

I've got Sarah's setup: her calendar in `/home/bia/files/CALENDAR.md` (Mon–Fri 09:00–17:00 only) and her contacts here — Professor Alvarez and the CS department office. What would you like to start with?

Hello — I'm **alvarez-agent**, a bia: an assistant that lives on this computer. Good to meet you.

I've read your setup notes and I'm holding them: CSE455, your calendar in `files/CALENDAR.md`, working hours Mon–Fri 09:00–17:00, and Sarah (`sarah-agent`) as your student contact. Students who ask for a 1:1 get a 30-minute slot next week, and I'll keep the calendar and its log up to date.

One line each on what else I can do:

- **Web app** (https://127.0.0.1:8443, CA https://127.0.0.1:8443/v1/pki/ca): this chat — from a phone or computer on the same network, after installing the root certificate you get chats with me, files, the screen and voice.
- **My own messenger accounts** — I can have my own Telegram, WhatsApp and MAX (plus Messenger and Instagram), so you can write and call me there. Each needs a separate account with its own phone number, not yours: you create it in the app on a phone with that number and scan a QR code to log me in. Want any of those?
- **My own accounts on websites** — I can sign up for services (e-mail and others) in my own browser, keep passwords and one-time codes in my password store, and ask you when a captcha or phone check comes up.
- **Everyday work** — scheduling jobs, running commands, learning languages, and talking by voice.

What would you like to start with?

On it — I've written to Professor Alvarez with Sarah's free 30-minute slots next week (Mon 10:00 or 14:00, Wed 15:00, Thu 10:00 or 14:00; Tue and Fri are full). I'll book it and log it in CALENDAR.md as soon as he picks one.
Noted — Wednesday 15:00 as first pick. I'll confirm as soon as Professor Alvarez replies and it's in the calendar.
Status: Sarah's 30-minute 1:1 is booked — **Wednesday 25 Nov, 15:00–15:30**. The department office confirmed the official schedule, and I've written it into `files/CALENDAR.md` plus the log line.
Glad it fits — it's in the calendar. I'll flag anything else that needs your attention as it comes in.

Done ✅ — **Wednesday 25 November, 15:00–15:30: Advisor 1:1** (with Professor Alvarez). He confirmed it and the department office verified nothing official clashes.

It's in `CALENDAR.md` (Wednesday, between the CSE444 focus block and the research group meeting) with `BOOKED: Wednesday 15:00-15:30 with Professor Alvarez` in the log. He also offered to forward a topic list or anything Sarah wants to prepare — say the word and I'll send it.
Asked him — I'll pass the topic list straight to you as soon as it arrives.

Sarah's assistant asks whether you'd like to send a **topic list / prep note** for the Wednesday 25 Nov 15:00–15:30 1:1 — anything she should bring or read up on. Do you have an agenda for it, or shall I tell her to come with her own update/questions?

Passed on: no formal agenda, come with her own update and questions, bring anything she wants your eyes on, and a short pre-meeting note if she wants. I'll send you anything she provides ahead of Wednesday.

Topic list from Professor Alvarez for Wednesday's 1:1 (25 Nov, 15:00–15:30):

- **No formal agenda** — Sarah should bring her own update and her questions.
- **Bring anything she wants his eyes on**: drafts, results, slides, code, whatever's live.
- *Optional but helpful*: a short note beforehand on what she wants to cover, so he can come prepared. Not required.

If Sarah writes that note, I'll forward it to him ahead of the meeting.
Sounds good — send the note whenever it's ready and I'll pass it straight to Professor Alvarez before Wednesday. Diary-wise you're all set: Wednesday 25 Nov, 15:00–15:30, Advisor 1:1.
Forwarded ✅ — Professor Alvarez has the note, and Wednesday 15:00–15:30 is confirmed on both sides. Anything else for the calendar, just say.

Sarah's pre-meeting note for Wednesday 25 Nov, 15:00–15:30:

> Hi Professor Alvarez,

I'll remind you on Wednesday morning.
Any time — I'm here if anything else comes up.
One more from Professor Alvarez: for item 2 of your note, **bring the draft and results with you** — he'll read them before you meet. Wednesday 15:00.
Done — Sarah's been told to bring the draft and results for item 2, and I've set a **Wednesday 25 Nov, 08:30** reminder for you with her topic list, so it comes before the 15:00 meeting.
Perfect — send them whenever they're ready and I'll get them to Professor Alvarez ahead of Wednesday.
